title: Tree DFS: return values up
summary: Diameter of a binary tree: the most edges on any path between two nodes. A post-order helper returns each subtree's height and records the best path through the current node on the way up. O(n). The TreeNode class is shown, not typed.
code: # Each call returns a height; the best path through a node joins both heights.
triggers: an answer for the whole tree built from answers for its subtrees
a path that may bend at any node: combine the left and right results there
prompts: Reporting lines form a tree in which each manager has at most two direct reports. How many reporting links separate the two people who are farthest apart?
A cave system branches like a binary tree from its entrance, and passages never rejoin. Counting passages, how long is the longest route between any two chambers?
invariant: height(node) returns the number of nodes on the longest downward path from node, and best is the longest path, in edges, through any node finished so far.
mantra: Return the height up; record left + right on the way.
pitfalls: What a call returns (height) differs from what it records (diameter): keep both straight.
Diameter counts edges: left + right, not left + right + 1.
Use nonlocal, or a one-element list, to update best from the nested function.
A deep, one-sided tree can hit Python's recursion limit of about 1000.

anchors.name: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
anchors.trick: Only the returned height: 1 + max(left, right).

anchors.name: Balanced Binary Tree
anchors.trick: Return the height, or -1 once the two sides differ by more than 1.

anchors.name: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
anchors.trick: Return value + the better non-negative side; record value + both non-negative sides.

mutations.explanation: Never counts the current node, so every height is 0 and the diameter is always 0.
Counts nodes instead of edges: a single node reports 1 instead of 0.
